**Answer:** One of the most celebrated and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser)** by French artist **Auguste Rodin**, completed in 1889. --- ### Why “The Kiss” stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin (1840–1917), a leading figure of modern sculpture | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast) – part of Rodin’s larger “The Gates of Hell” project | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist blend; dynamic, sensual form | | **Material** | Bronze (originally marble, later bronze casts) | | **Iconography** | A passionate embrace between two lovers, capturing movement and emotion | | **Cultural Impact** | • Became a symbol of romantic love and artistic freedom.
• Inspired countless reproductions, adaptations, and scholarly debates.
• Frequently referenced in literature, film, and popular culture. | --- ### Context within the 19th‑Century Sculpture Landscape - **Other notable 19th‑century works**: - *The Gates of Hell* (1880–1917) – a monumental bronze group by Rodin. - *The Thinker* (1902–1904) – technically early 20th, but often associated with Rodin’s legacy. - *The Statue of Liberty* (1886) – a monumental public monument. - **Why “The Kiss” is often singled out**: - It captures the era’s shift toward expressive realism. - Its intimate scale contrasts with the grand public monuments of the time, making it accessible and relatable. - The work’s influence on subsequent generations of sculptors and its presence in museums worldwide cement its status as a cultural icon. --- ### Quick Reference - **Title**: The Kiss (Le Baiser) - **Artist**: Auguste Rodin - **Year**: 1889 (first cast) - **Medium**: Bronze (originally marble) - **Location**: Various casts worldwide (e.g., Musée Rodin, Paris; National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.) --- **Bottom line:** While many masterpieces were produced during the 19th century, Rodin’s *The Kiss* is frequently cited as the most famous sculpture of that period due to its artistic innovation, emotional depth, and enduring popularity.
